text:
alyssa: noticing weird token-stream jitter from cross-rack gpu pools this morning, several streaming RPCs hit deadline spikes ~200-400ms

darren: saw that too, traces show reordering and a bunch of retransmits between rack A and B

sasha: packet reorder, not loss? NIC counters show reorders + a spike in out-of-order acks on igb0

matt: confirmed, kernel drop stats are low but `netstat -s` shows TCP: reord packets up, also a couple NIC firmware warnings earlier

alyssa: symptoms: streaming clients get partial tokens then pause, KV cache stays fine, so it's likely transport-level reordering affecting in-flight token batches

darren: affects deadlines because our runtime uses tight per-request rpc_timeouts (50-100ms tail buffer). If reorder delays first bytes, grpc deadline hits

sasha: tried increasing deadline on a canary route to 300ms, tail improved but overall p99 latency still noisy

matt: can we repro with iperf3/tcpdump between two pods in different racks? I can spin up containers and run `sudo tc qdisc` checks

alyssa: please run `tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/reorder.pcap 'tcp port 12345'` and iperf3 in reverse mode for 5m, record MSS/MTU

oncall-bot: deploy 1847 -> infra/gpu-pool-bump applied to two nodes (rolling) :package:

darren: quick mitigation: we rolled back a recent kernel NIC offload change in rackB yesterday, trying to toggle GRO/LRO off on affected hosts (`ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off lro off`)

sasha: toggling off GRO reduced reorder spikes in short tests, but CPU overhead increases — can't keep that on everywhere

alyssa: long term options: 1) ensure MTU alignment across leaf switches and hosts (found earlier mismatch in us-west2-azc), 2) firmware upgrade for Broadcom NICs, 3) kernel tuning (tcp_retries2, bbr pacing), 4) move latency-sensitive streaming to same-rack pools

matt: also consider enabling RDMA for intra-rack model traffic where available; RDMA avoids TCP head-of-line for our RPCs and reduces jitter

darren: cost/regional implications: moving workloads to same-rack pools will reduce capacity flexibility — need capacity plan if we pin traffic to racks for SLOs

sasha: can we add short-term autoscale buffers? e.g., allow burst capacity in same-rack pool during peak to avoid cross-rack spills

alyssa: action items: 1) matt to capture pcap + iperf results and NIC counters (due in 2h), 2) darren to roll GRO/LRO toggle across canary hosts and measure CPU/cost impact, 3) sasha to draft deployment option for rack-local streaming pools and estimate capacity delta

matt: starting captures now, will upload pcap and perf graphs to the thread

darren: toggling on 3 hosts now, posting observations in ~30m :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sasha: drafting capacity plan, will include cost delta and fallback routing policy (auto-fallback to slightly larger model variant if cross-rack latency spikes)

alyssa: good. if anyone sees reorders in other regions, ping me directly. Also linking the trace from a bad request: https://internal-traces/redwood/trace/0xdeadbeef

oncall-bot: alert: high-rpc-deadlines in us-west2-gpu-pool detected (10:12 UTC) — suppressed after mitigation rollouts

alyssa: thanks team, prioritize the pcap and canary metrics. we'll decide on firmware vs config after data. :white_check_mark:
